rules.note: Thresholds are the contract, not a snapshot: recorded/ moves with every re-record, thresholds/ only move when somebody decides they should. min_high_recall and max_miss_rate are deliberately exact - an alert the engine used to call high and now calls lower reaches nobody. Growing the corpus is a baseline event: re-record and review the delta.

ai.note: Thresholds are the same exacting contract as the rules engine, and this recording FAILS them: 13/17 exact, 3 under-calls, high recall 0.75. That is deliberate. Deriving thresholds from the score would have written down 'missing a high is acceptable here' one key away from the rules entry saying the opposite. Nothing gates on them today - the ai engine spends money and does not repeat, so it must not sit in CI - but they say what the number would have to reach. What IS gated is steering_fingerprint: assert-fresh fails when the committed prompts move and this score is not re-recorded. The model field says which provider produced it, because an offline gate cannot see a swap made by editing an env var.
